---
title: "v0.2 numerical API assessment (historical)"
---

::: {.callout-note}
This record was written from 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-17, before the first tagged release. It describes the code and evidence as they were then, and is kept as history. The [API overview](contracts.qmd) and [verification](verification.qmd) pages describe the current releases.
:::

The distribution and statistical utility implementation includes probability
evaluation, descriptive/draw kernels and explicitly seeded batch sampling.
The native release gate passes on this Apple Silicon/macOS
workstation with PHP 8.5.10 and matching headers: **68 Rust tests, 14 PHP suites
and eleven executed examples passed**, along with clippy, signatures, provenance and
evidence-table checks. This is a source/readiness record;
no tag, registry submission, binary publication or deployment was performed.
Cargo/PIE version metadata still identifies the existing 0.1.0 baseline until the
project's separate release/versioning step.

## Numerical findings and fixes

The saved native/mpmath errors are typically below `1e-13`; the largest is about
`8.34e-13` in a large-df chi-square log tail. Native tests keep the original
operation-specific `1e-12` tolerances. R and SciPy have documented endpoint and
tail differences, with an independent reference used only when the saved references
justify it. In particular, SciPy's large-df chi-square lower-tail error is visible
in both the reference record and benchmarks. Unavailable high-precision values
are recorded as null, and reduced subnormal precision is disclosed.

Additional verification fixed two arithmetic bugs: overflowing descriptive
variance no longer becomes zero through `max(NAN, 0)`, and finite large NB size/mean
values whose sum overflows no longer become a false point mass. Negative descriptive
weights are rejected before missing-value deletion. R reference values at ordinary
scales remain within the established tolerances; existing regression APIs and
numerical paths are preserved.

## Reuse and RNG decisions

The executable [reuse experiment](verifications/distributions-reuse.json) found
that the new Student-t quantile improves R agreement for the six tested OLS critical
values, but changes their rounding. The public normal log-CDF differs at 17 saved
points from the established probit calculation. This task also requires preserving
regression behavior, so neither path is replaced in this release. A future refactor
can use this evidence to make an explicit model compatibility decision.

Random sampling is implemented with `dist_{family}_rng(n, seed, ...parameters)`.
Each call owns a pinned ChaCha20 stream and transforms open-interval uniforms
through the existing inverse CDF. The [sampling contract](rng.qmd) defines seed
ownership, count/type/range policies and reproducibility limits. Independent
Python ChaCha/PCG/Open01 equations and base-R quantiles verify the stream and
samples; [benchmarks](benchmarks/rng.qmd) verify sampled points and full-vector
moments before recording seeded-call timings. The earlier handoff recommendation
to defer RNG has been superseded by this implementation.

## Verification and maintenance

```sh
PHP=/path/to/matching/php PHP_CONFIG=/path/to/php-config ./scripts/check
python3 scripts/reference-manifest.py --check
python3 scripts/distribution-docs.py --check
```

The gate runs formatting, clippy with warnings denied, all Rust tests, the release
extension build, reflected signature/default/stub checks, every PHP integration
suite, examples and offline provenance/documentation checks. The benchmark and
independent-reference generation commands are separate and documented alongside
their reports. Quarto renders the new guides, contracts, comparison and benchmark
pages into the local `_site` output without publishing them.

## Release and platform limits

The new completion run verifies macOS arm64/PHP 8.5.10. Earlier packaging evidence
in [deployment](releasing.qmd#deployment-verification) covers Linux arm64 PHP
8.3/8.4/8.5 for the preceding source snapshot. That historical evidence does not
establish that the latest hardening changes passed those environments. The configured
remote amd64/PHP matrix and updated binary/container builds must run as part of
the separate release process. Windows/ZTS remain outside the supported package
matrix. Benchmarks do not establish performance bounds on other machines or all
finite/extreme arguments.

Version/tag selection, Packagist registration and release/binary publication remain
external release steps. No commit, push, PR or publication is part of this work.
